79: Amplifications and restrictions - [in his method of exegesis,] the specification is not taken as what is meant by the generalization -- that is, you should not say the general term only includes that which is in the specification. Rather, it comes to restrict -- the general term would have included everything, and the restriction comes afterwards to indicate that this, and things similar to it, were what I meant for you by the generalization. Therefore, even if [the verse] does not go on to state another generalization, I would have [known that the rule applies only] to bring things that are similar to the specification. If the verse then goes on to amplify again, it comes to amplify [and include] everything, and there is only one thing excluded. It was given over to the Rabbis to decided which thing was fit to be removed from the generalization. Thus "restriction" is interpreted to mean "restricted somewhat from its connotation."
